title: Spin Birefringence and Spin Polarized Transmission across p-wave Altermagnetic Heterostructure
abstract: This paper investigates electron transport properties across N/AM interface or N/AM/N heterojunction. Based on Hamiltonians in the three regions, general wave functions are proposed and combined linear equations are constructed. Reflection and transmission coefficients as well as spin polarizatioin of the altermagnet heterostructure are obtained. When electron incident from normal metal to altermagnet, it is scattered and split into + branch and _ branch transmitting into altermagnet zone with separate refractive angles. Total internal reflection might happen to + branch. Critical angle of total reflection is determined by incident conditions and properties of AM material. In the heterostructure case, spin-up and spin-down electrons transmitted with same propagation directions but different transmission probabilities. Transmission and polarization periodically change with length of the junction. Exchange field and spin-splitting strength have pronounced effect on spin-polarized transmittance while the effect of spin-orbit coupling is quite small. Optimized system can be found by tuning parameters of the AM material. This study will lay the theoretical groundwork for experimental research on spin-selective outputs and spintronic devices.
summary: This theoretical work analyzes electron transport through p-wave altermagnetic heterostructures, focusing on spin birefringence and spin-polarized transmission. By solving coupled wave equations, the authors demonstrate that spin-up and spin-down electrons experience different transmission probabilities, leading to tunable spin-selective outputs. This lays the groundwork for all-electrical spintronic functionality.
main_problem: The paper investigates spin birefringence and spin-polarized electron transport across p-wave Altermagnetic (AM) heterostructures.
main_result: The study shows that spin-up and spin-down electrons transmit with different probabilities, and the transmission and polarization periodically change with the length of the junction.
method: The authors used a theoretical approach involving constructing combined linear equations from general wave functions derived from the Hamiltonian in the three distinct regions (N/AM/N).
model_or_system: The system is a heterostructure composed of a Normal metal (N) region / p-wave Altermagnetic (AM) region / Normal metal (N) region. The AM region is modeled using a low-energy effective Hamiltonian exhibiting pure electronic nonrelativistic spin-splitting.
key_observables: Reflection and transmission coefficients, spin polarization of the altermagnet heterostructure, and spin-birefringence effects.
important_parameters: Junction length (d), incident angle ($	heta_i$), spin-splitting strength ($p$), and exchange field strength ($m_z$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes ballistic transport and approximates the N regions as a 2D semi-infinite electron gas.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic N/AM/N structure, and subsequent figures show the periodic variation of transmission and polarization as a function of junction length (d), incident angle ($	heta_i$), and material parameters.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework by defining Hamiltonians for the three regions, solving for wave functions, and then applying boundary conditions to derive transmission and reflection coefficients, analyzing the dependence on various physical parameters.
why_interesting: The study provides a detailed theoretical framework for controlling spin-selective electron transport using intrinsic magnetic order, which is highly relevant for designing next-generation spintronic devices.
